items.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I started playing with Jimmy and Jeannie Cheatham

ctx.x: I started playing with Jimmy and Jeannie Cheatham, Jimmy and Jeannie Cheatham, I started playing with them, in fact, I got them on the Tonight Show one time. And they came on the Tonight Show and I played with them on the Tonight Show. That was a good act, I mean, they had a good thing, she sang the blues and he played the trombone, yeah he played trombone and he wrote music and he had a little thing together and I worked with him. I helped them out a lot because me playing in that group, I think it was…what was…
Not that one, no. On Record, I heard them on record but not live.

items.title: Jimmy and Jeannie Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: See if we know it’s Snooky, then he knows certain things that help support what Snooky does. Right?

ctx.x: Well actually, fundamentally, I’m a firm believer in going into the aspect of the intuitive side for utmost, as far as the intellectual part, I mean given the scientific lean and the voice of notes and things like that. Because even intuitively, I get sounds that I hear, and when I hear it then I go—
And it depends on who’s solo. See if we know it’s Snooky, then he knows certain things that help support what Snooky does. Right?

Yeah and then writing, like when we do the group sounds and things like that, and Jeannie’s background, when we’re playing for Jeannie, there’s a certain nuance that happens, in terms of everybody. So that we just get that wonderful, how can I say it, homogeneous —
